description:
MATERIAL. Every token is a pure line drawing: unfilled outlines, uniform thin-to-medium stroke, no gradients, no raster texture, no type. The ground is a flat near-black with a slight warm cast, identical in all twelve. Only two ink colours are ever used — a bone/parchment cream and a cool slate blue-grey — plus the occasional dimmed, semi-transparent version of either, which is how depth is made: the faint shapes read as being behind the bright ones. There is no third hue anywhere on the sheets.

WHAT IT IS A PICTURE OF. Nothing representational. It reads as drafted geometry — a compass-and-straightedge construction, a rose window, a ritual seal, an architectural plan rotated on itself. The vocabulary is small and strictly held: squares, hexagons, circles, and diamonds, either (a) nested concentrically, a square inside a square inside a dot, or (b) copied and rotated in a ring around a shared centre to make a star or rosette, or (c) one large enclosing container — a big square, a big circle, a big hexagon — with the smaller machinery sitting inside or on it. Around most of them a scatter of small satellite polygons drifts off the main body, some of them nested miniatures of the central motif.

WHAT THE TWELVE SHARE. Centred, roughly circular mass; one dominant enclosing figure; rotational repetition; the same two-ink palette; the same stroke weight; the same habit of a small nested detail dropped inside a large empty shape. Laid out together they are unmistakably one hand and one system.

HOW THEY DIFFER. Overwhelmingly by DENSITY and by SYMMETRY ORDER, and the density spread is very wide. Dense to the point of texture: 9190 (interior is a tangled cream scribble of dozens of small squares inside a rotated-square star), 9548 (a thick ring of small squares orbiting a slate rosette), 10980 (a full mandala — circle, star, ring of squares, square frame, all at once), 10264 (an overlapping swirl of large translucent squares). Middle: 9011, 9727, 9906, 10622. Nearly empty: 10085 (one large slate square, one large cream hexagon, one small nested square, three dots — that is the entire token), 10443 (a cream diamond containing a slate hexagon containing three tiny circles, plus two small squares outside), 9369 (two large thin rings at left with tiny circles nested in them, over a dim, barely-visible square rosette), 10801 (one big slate square frame with a handful of pale squares scattered at the corners). Symmetry order also varies: 9906 is a clean 6-fold snowflake, 9727 reads 5-fold, 9011 and 9548 8-to-12-fold, while 10622, 10801 and 10264 are deliberately asymmetric scatters with no rotational centre at all.

THE THREE STATES. The change is a single, legible axis: SCALE and DENSITY, i.e. the figure breathing in and out. NEUTRAL is the reference. STRESS contracts — the whole drawing shrinks toward the centre, sheds its outer material and its satellites, and leaves a wide black margin: 9190 stress collapses from an edge-filling scribble to a small pale rosette inside a thin dark square, 9011 stress becomes a bare slate star outline with a small cream knot in the middle and far more emptiness than ink, 9369 stress shrinks its big ring to about half the frame and drops most of its little circles, 9548 stress loses its whole outer ring of squares. RECOVERY does the opposite and overshoots neutral — larger, denser, more elements, more overlap, pressing to the tile edge: 9190 recovery fills the tile corner to corner, 9548 recovery re-grows the square ring thicker than neutral, 9369 recovery blows the main circle up until it nearly touches the bottom of the tile and stacks a third satellite ring on the left, 9011 recovery adds a second outer square frame and runs off the left edge. Hue barely moves; stress leans a touch cooler and greyer because the cream detail is what gets removed, but that is a by-product of the shrink, not a separate colour move.

TOKEN IDENTITY ACROSS STATES. Preserved. Same seed in all three rows keeps its motif, its symmetry order, its colour assignment and its layout — 9369 is the two-rings-and-a-ghost-rosette token in all three, 9906-style hexagonal logic never turns into circle logic. It is one object photographed at three exposures, not three objects.

AT 120PX. Nine of the twelve survive as distinct silhouettes: the dense ones (9190, 9548, 10264, 10980) become texture-blobs but each has its own outline shape, and the mid ones (9011, 9727, 9906, 10443, 10622) keep a readable icon. Three go weak: 9369 is a pair of thin grey outlines on black and nearly disappears, 10085 reads as an almost blank tile with a wire hexagon in it, and 10801 reads as an empty square. On the 120 state sheet the state change survives easily — stress tiles are visibly small, quiet objects marooned in black; recovery tiles are visibly bigger and pushed to the tile border — but 9369 stress at 120 is close to nothing at all.

ARTIFACTS I CAN SEE. Elements cross or touch the tile boundary in several recovery frames (9011 recovery on the left edge, 9190 recovery on all four) and in a couple of neutral seeds (9727 has a small diamond bisected by the right edge; 10622 and 10801 push squares into the corners). 9190's neutral and recovery interiors are so dense they lose their individual squares and turn into a woven grey mush. Nothing looks broken or half-rendered otherwise; strokes are clean, joins are clean, there is no aliasing damage even at 120.
